scope: Development evidence, not final release acceptance

gaps.section: 9. As-built versus target: tracked UX gaps and required closure
contract: Production owner Save succeeded but automatic Spanish preparation failed twice; UI only said provider unavailable. `draftProgramSpanish` catches provider/parse/validator errors together.
Diagnose exact production source using protected instrumentation; stage-specific error handling and successful exact-source end-to-end; no owner retry until server-side proof.
gaps.before: Production owner Save succeeded but automatic Spanish preparation failed twice; UI only said provider unavailable. `draftProgramSpanish` catches provider/parse/validator errors together.
gaps.after: Exact-source OpenAI executions and persisted seven-field readback pass. Provider, timeout, malformed response and semantic failures remain separately actionable.

gaps.section: 9. As-built versus target: tracked UX gaps and required closure
contract: Previously multiple “succeeded” Participant Page versions with missing seven Spanish fields.
Complete validation *before* marking ready/generating current; no redundant incomplete artifacts; current material readback.
gaps.before: Previously multiple “succeeded” Participant Page versions with missing seven Spanish fields.
gaps.after: Incomplete bilingual Page is labeled as a draft; Update preserves the current Summary, creates only a complete affected Page, and retries reuse the completed operation.

gaps.section: 9. As-built versus target: tracked UX gaps and required closure
contract: Start section had been hidden if current Participant Page missing; PR #265 now shows blocked Final Review heading, but actual owner launch remains unaccepted.
Prove actual authenticated current materials → one confirmation → enabled action and protected launch in isolated real application, then owner verifies Production.
gaps.before: Start section had been hidden if current Participant Page missing; PR #265 now shows blocked Final Review heading, but actual owner launch remains unaccepted.
gaps.after: One version-bound review and protected idempotent publication pass in the isolated application. Production owner acceptance remains pending an authorized finished release.

gaps.section: 9. As-built versus target: tracked UX gaps and required closure
contract: External-rights predicate previously counted Partner Admin membership/`not_required` metadata as third-party authority; PR #263 corrected that path.
Keep regression for legacy test workspace transition to LegalEase-managed without forged consent, preserve genuine external rights.
gaps.before: External-rights predicate previously counted Partner Admin membership/`not_required` metadata as third-party authority; PR #263 corrected that path.
gaps.after: Membership alone no longer invents third-party operating rights. Actual agreement-protected configuration changes remain refused.

gaps.section: 9. As-built versus target: tracked UX gaps and required closure

Verify both ordinary and access-code sessions against entire effective approved jurisdiction set, and Clinic event state boundary.
gaps.before: Multi-state program permission and screening claim are separate backend boundaries; current policy requires cross-layer consistency.
gaps.after: Program state sets persist across roles; ordinary/code intake and Clinic assistance enforce their actual scope, including direct-request denials.

gaps.section: 9. As-built versus target: tracked UX gaps and required closure
contract: Platform Admin editor exposes a large registry-driven form with many routine and exceptional values.
Progressive disclosure around operator, geography, services, languages; save once and direct to Preview.
gaps.before: Platform Admin editor exposes a large registry-driven form with many routine and exceptional values.
gaps.after: Configure uses grouped fields and one canonical Save; its immediate Review Program Materials action opens the authoritative previews.

gaps.section: 9. As-built versus target: tracked UX gaps and required closure
contract: Source retains both provisioning/new and onboarding/new creation UIs.
One canonical creation route, preserve underlying records and aliases, safe redirect other URL.
gaps.before: Source retains both provisioning/new and onboarding/new creation UIs.
gaps.after: One canonical creation flow retains the old route as a compatibility redirect. Exact creation replay does not duplicate the program.

gaps.section: 9. As-built versus target: tracked UX gaps and required closure
contract: Admin diagnostics has numerous business/agreement forms that visually look like launch prerequisites.
Clearly advanced-only and directly resolve actual applicable contractual work, not required for LegalEase-managed screening-only.
gaps.before: Admin diagnostics has numerous business/agreement forms that visually look like launch prerequisites.
gaps.after: Managed screening launches from the workspace. Applicable external arrangements link directly to scoped diagnostics; fake executed agreements are refused.

gaps.section: 9. As-built versus target: tracked UX gaps and required closure

Allow permitted multistate configuration and truthful readback within partner delegation, server-enforced.
gaps.before: Partner five-step `ProgramOnboarding` currently offers a one-state picker while Platform Admin supports multistate.
gaps.after: The Partner selects multiple permitted jurisdictions through checkboxes and receives authoritative refresh/readback. Forged jurisdictions are denied.

gaps.section: 9. As-built versus target: tracked UX gaps and required closure

One source-matched bilingual preparation/review workflow respecting partner-specific claims and genuine partner sign-off where required.
gaps.before: Partner-managed Spanish step CURRENT presents seven required fields.
gaps.after: Partner preparation uses real source-matched OpenAI output for custom public copy and approved Spanish for standard fields; no manual seven-field assignment.

gaps.section: 9. As-built versus target: tracked UX gaps and required closure

Accurate labels, role-safe dedicated views when actually implemented; no fake exports or private Briefcase.
gaps.before: Partner reporting and participants pages currently reuse aggregate dashboard; legacy reporting says export unavailable.
gaps.after: Activity & Reporting is accurately labeled, tenant-scoped and aggregate-only. It does not advertise a fabricated export or participant-owned Briefcase.

gaps.section: 9. As-built versus target: tracked UX gaps and required closure

gaps.after: Interrupted reset remains locked; actual server revocation, BFCache/back navigation and a second authenticated participant show no previous-participant leakage.

gaps.after: Creation stays draft; real event prerequisites and lifecycle apply. Capacity is not funding. Positive funded sponsorship acceptance is blocked by the absence of genuinely funded isolated evidence.

gaps.section: 9. As-built versus target: tracked UX gaps and required closure

gaps.after: The canonical public CTA is action-sized; partner custom translation reuses an approved concise bilingual CTA without silently replacing custom prose.
